question: After narrowing the target to the end of juan 16 and nearby target-table leaves, what current official NLC routes lawfully support requesting a surrogate/reproduction of call 14202 without falsely claiming that a request has been submitted or accepted?
answer: Current NLC first-party service pages expose three complementary lawful routes: (1) the Rare Books & Special Collections Reading Room for closed-stack consultation, with originals generally withheld when microfilm/digital/photocopy surrogates exist; (2) the Document Supply Center, which publicly accepts document requests by online system, email, phone, fax or on-site and offers scanning, photography and microfilm restoration among its services; and (3) the National Microfilming Center's document consultation/supply and digital restoration services for rare and other documents. This batch turns call 14202 into a precise request payload, but does not submit it. Submission/acceptance, identity/card requirements, permissions, pricing and actual deliverability of this rare-book item remain external-service decisions.
